RAL HYAKUTAKE TO CALL ON CHIANG KAI SHEK 


It is reported that at the 
request of Chiang Kai Shek, Vice-Admiral Hyakutake, 
Commander-in-Chief of the Third Fleet, will meet Chiang 
Kei Shek at Chungking on June 6. It is believed that 
the north China affair will be discussed at the conference. 

It appeaggthat the withdrawal 
of the I7th Army comprising of two Divisions, and the 
dissolution of the Kuomintang, the Blue Shirts Society 
and the C. Ce Corps, which had been demanded by the 
Kwantung Arny have not been Feported to Chiang Kai Shek 
owing to fear of Chiang Kai “hek on the part of the 
Chinese authorities in the North. ‘Pue to this with- 
holding of information Chiang Kai Shek has not been 
able to understand the true situation and frame his 
policy properly. Chiang Kai Shek's object in asking 
for a conference with Admiral Hyakutake is to learn the 
true intentions of the Japanese army in the north China 
affaire It is expected that the Admiral will frankly 
explain Japan's intentions so that Chiang Kai Shek can 
understand the situation clearly. Great importance is 
being attached to the conference because it will assist 
Chiang Kai Shek to frame his policy.

December 3, 1935.
Afternoon Translation.

MAINICHI

JAPANESE ADMIRALS TO BE ENTERTAINED

Yesterday the Japanese Navy Office issued orders to the effect that Vice Admiral Hyakutake, Commander of the Third Fleet, will be promoted to commander of the Sasebo Naval Base, Rear-Admiral Sugisaka, Commander of the IIth Squadron on the Yantze, will be assigned for duty with the General Naval Staff, and Rear-Admiral Araki, Commander of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, will be made chief of the Defence Corps of Yokosuka.

At 6 p.m. December 6 local Japanese residents will entertain the above high naval officials who are leaving Shanghai and Rear-Admiral Kondo who became Commander of the Special Naval Landing Party, at the Japanese Club.

At 6.30 p.m. December 7 Vice-Admiral Hyakutake, Rear-Admirals Sugisaka, Araki and Kondo will entertain local Japanese officials and important civilians at the Japanese Club.

ARRIVAL OF VICE-ADMIRAL OIKAWA

Vice-Admiral Oikawa, new Commander of the Third Fleet, will arrive in Shanghai at 3 p.m. December 8.

DEPARTURE OF ADMIRALS

Vice-Admiral Hyakutake, Rear-Admirals Sugisaka and Araki, will leave here at 9 a.m. December 9 on the S. S. Nagasaki Maru.

REAR-ADMIRAL KONDO TO CALL ON LOCAL JAPANESE OFFICIALS

Rear-Admiral Kondo received a government order yesterday appointing him Commander of the Special Naval Landing Party in Shanghai. He will call round all local Japanese officials to inform them of his appointment.

HEARING OF FRAUD CHARGE AGAINST A JAPANESE

The hearing of a fraud charge which was filed against a Japanese named R. Furukawa, age 67, residing at 86, Lane 53, Woosung Road, will be held at the Japanese Consular Court at 9 a.m. to-day.

GEN. HO YING CHIN PROCEEDS TO THE NORTH WITH FIVE MILLION DOLLARS TO BRIBE OFFICIALS.

A Daito telegram from Peiping dated December 2 states that General Ho Ying Chin has proceeded to the North with $5,000,000 in Central Bank notes to bribe the militarists in the North.

1935年12月3日。
下午译文。

《每日新闻》

款待日本海军将领

昨日，日本海军省发布命令，内容如下：第三舰队司令百武（Hyakutake）海军中将晋升为佐世保海军基地司令；长江第11战队司令杉坂（Sugisaka）海军少将调任海军军令部任职；日本特别海军陆战队司令荒木（Araki）海军少将出任横须贺防卫团团长。

12月6日下午6时，当地日本居民将在日本总会宴请即将离沪的上述海军高级官员，以及新任特别海军陆战队司令近藤（Kondo）海军少将。

12月7日下午6时30分，百武海军中将，杉坂、荒木及近藤海军少将将在日本总会宴请当地日本官员及重要平民。

及川（Oikawa）海军中将抵达

新任第三舰队司令及川（Oikawa）海军中将将于12月8日下午3时抵达上海。

海军将领离沪

百武海军中将，杉坂及荒木海军少将，将于12月9日上午9时乘坐“长崎丸”号（S. S. Nagasaki Maru）离开此地。

近藤海军少将拜会当地日本官员

近藤海军少将昨日收到政府任命其为上海特别海军陆战队司令的命令。他将拜访所有当地日本官员，通报其任命事宜。

审理针对一名日本人的欺诈指控

针对居住在吴淞路53弄86号、67岁的日本人R. Furukawa提出的欺诈指控，将于今日上午9时在日本领事法庭开庭审理。

何应钦将军携五百万元北上贿赂官员。

据12月2日发自北平的大同社电称，何应钦将军已携带中央银行钞票五百万元前往北方，以贿赂北方的军阀。

（左侧手写批注：）

June 5, 1935. Morning Translation.

MAINICHI

D3104 ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE TO CALL ON CHIANG KAI SHEK

It is reported that at the request of Chiang Kai Shek, Vice-Admiral Hyakutake, Commander-in-Chief of the Third Fleet, will meet Chiang Kai Shek at Chungking on June 6. It is believed that the north China affair will be discussed at the conference.

It appears that the withdrawal of the 17th Army comprising of two Divisions, and the dissolution of the Kuomintang, the Blue Shirts Society and the C. C. Corps, which had been demanded by the Kwantung Army have not been reported to Chiang Kai Shek owing to fear of Chiang Kai Shek on the part of the Chinese authorities in the North. Due to this withholding of information Chiang Kai Shek has not been able to understand the true situation and frame his policy properly. Chiang Kai Shek's object in asking for a conference with Admiral Hyakutake is to learn the true intentions of the Japanese army in the north China affair. It is expected that the Admiral will frankly explain Japan's intentions so that Chiang Kai Shek can understand the situation clearly. Great importance is being attached to the conference because it will assist Chiang Kai Shek to frame his policy.

1935年6月5日。上午译文。

《每日新闻》

D3104 百武海军中将将会见蒋介石

据报道，应蒋介石之邀，第三舰队司令百武（Hyakutake）海军中将将于6月6日在重庆会见蒋介石。据悉，会议将讨论华北事件。

看来，关东军曾要求撤走由两个师团组成的第17军，并解散国民党、蓝衣社和CC系，但由于中国北方当局对蒋介石心存畏惧，未将这些要求报告给蒋介石。由于这种信息封锁，蒋介石未能了解真实情况并制定恰当的政策。蒋介石要求与百武海军中将举行会议的目的，是为了了解日本军队在华北事件中的真实意图。预计该海军中将坦率说明日本的意图，以便蒋介石清楚地了解局势。此次会议备受重视，因为它将有助于蒋介石制定政策。

MAINICHI

VICE-ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE ARRIVES IN SHANGHAI

Vice-Admiral Hyakutake,
the new Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese Third Fleet,
arrived in Shanghai yesterday on the flagship "Idzumo".
After receiving Japanese visitors on the flagship, the
Admiral landed at 2.30 P.M. and visited Japanese

Mayor Wu of the Shanghai City Government, Lieutenant-

A Rengo telegram from Tokyo
dated December 5 reports that the Tokyo Foreign Office
having learned that Mr. Kishimoto, Commissioner of the
Chinese Customs, will be transferred from the Office
of the Inspector-General of the Chinese Customs to the
Tientsin Customs, will lodge a strong protest with
the Chinese Government against the transfer because it
will greatly affect Japan's trade policy in China.

Special Branch include the maintaining of a direct liaison
between this office and the local Japanese Naval Attache's
office in regard to the daily movements of this distinguished
personage. This advance information relating to his movements
is immediately submitted to the Deputy Commissioner (Special

(Japanese) and the various Divisional Officers concerned for
necessary action.

Naval Authorities have expressly desired that no Police escort
will be necessary to accompany the Admiral during the course
of his visits within the Settlement.

specially detailed posse of Police from Central Station were
on observation at the Customs Jetty. Furthermore members of
the Special Branch were also on duty at the Japanese Consulate-
General during the Admiral's visit to Mr. A. Ariyoshi, Japanese
Minister to China, and Mr. Ishii, Japanese Consul-General.

December 4, 1934. Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

NICHI-NICHI

VICE-ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE ARRIVING TO-MORROW

Vice-Admiral Hyakutake, the new Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese Third Fleet, will arrive in Shanghai at 10 a.m. to-morrow on the flagship "Idzumo" from the North. The flagship will moor at the naval buoy near the French Bund. The Admiral will leave here on December 9 for the South on a tour of inspection on his flagship.

The local Japanese naval authorities announce that Vice-Admiral Hyakutake will receive visitors, call on foreign officials and entertain local Japanese officials and civilians in accordance with the following programme:-

On the morning of December 5 Japanese naval officers will visit the flagship and later up to 2.30 p.m. other officials and civilians will call on the Admiral. After 2.30 p.m. the Admiral will land in Shanghai. A naval launch will be provided for the use of visitors at 1.30 p.m. and 2 p.m. from the Customs jetty.

On December 6 visits to foreign military and civil officials will be made.

On 7th and 8th the Admiral will inspect various Japanese warships.

On the evening of December 8, he will entertain local Japanese officials and civilians at the Japanese Club, Boone Road.

KOREAN GIRLS ARRESTED FOR PROSTITUTION

The Japanese Consular Police with the assistance of the S.M.P. arrested 4 Korean girls on December 1 at No. 177 Thibet Road on a charge of prostitution and on December 3 they were each fined five yen. A Korean male named Kim Kwan Kyo who was arrested at the same address for keeping a house of prostitution, will be tried later owing to the fact that he is now sick.

MAINICHI

VICE-ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE ARRIVES IN SHANGHAI

Vice-Admiral Hyakutake, the new Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese Third Fleet, arrived in Shanghai yesterday on the flagship "Idzumo". After receiving Japanese visitors on the flagship, the Admiral landed at 2.30 p.m. and visited Japanese Minister Ariyoshi, Japanese Consul-General Ishii, Mayor Wu of the Shanghai City Government, Lieutenant-General Suzuki, Military attache to the Japanese Legation, and Mr. Yasui, Chairman of the Executive Committee of the Japanese Residents Corporation.

JAPAN TO LODGE PROTEST WITH CHINA AGAINST TRANSFER OF A JAPANESE CUSTOMS COMMISSIONER

A Rengo telegram from Tokyo dated December 5 reports that the Tokyo Foreign Office having learned that Mr. Kishimoto, Commissioner of the Chinese Customs, will be transferred from the Office of the Inspector-General of the Chinese Customs to the Tientsin Customs, will lodge a strong protest with the Chinese Government against the transfer because it will greatly affect Japan's trade policy in China.

JAPANESE OPIUM ADDICT ARRESTED BY S.M.P.

A Japanese named J. Kakuya, age 32, was arrested together with a number of Chinese opium smokers by the S.M.P. when the latter raided a Chinese opium den at No. 36 Passage 306 Miller Road at 8 p.m. December 4 and was handed over to the Japanese Consular authorities.

MISCELLANEOUS

NIPPO

THREE KOREANS ARRESTED BY JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

Upon receiving information from the Korean Association in the Japanese Y.M.C.A., Range Road, at 3 p.m. yesterday to the effect that three Koreans were creating a disturbance there, the Japanese Consular Police immediately dispatched two constables to investigate the affair. The officers took three Koreans named Pak Chi Ho, age 37, residing at No. 565 Woosung Road, Lim Jun Bai, age 28, residing at No. 36 Chang An Lee, off Woosung Road, and Lee Shang Long, age 22, to the Japanese Consulate. The police investigation showed that the trio were present in the Association at the request of the latter to settle a dispute between them. The trouble in question was caused on the evening of December 2 when Lim and Lee visited Pak's home and stated that they were to search his home by order of the Korean Association. The search was made and they found 4 packages of heroin each containing one gram which they took away. An electric bell and some furniture was smashed during the search. Although Pak asked Lim and Lee to produce a police search warrant they did not do so.

Having been informed of the incident, Mr. Lee Young Ro, Vice President of the Korean Association requested the trio to come to the Association to settle the matter and it was then that Lee Shang Long started to make trouble. The Consular Police are making further investigations into the matter.

D. 3104.

JAPANESE RESIDENTS TO ENTERTAIN VICE-ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE

It is reported that the local Japanese residents will entertain Vice-Admiral Hyakutake, the new Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese Third Fleet, at 2 p.m. December 8 at the Japanese Rokusan Garden. Application for admission to the entertainment will be made at the Japanese Club and not more than 400 applications will be received.

JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE COMING TO SHANGHAI

Six Japanese police officers who have been recruited for the local Japanese Consular Police will arrive in Shanghai on December 7 on the S.S. Nagasaki Maru.

三名朝鲜人被日本领事警察逮捕

昨日午后3时，日本基督教青年会（位于兰路）内的朝鲜人协会通报称，有三名朝鲜人在该处滋事，日本领事警察随即派遣两名巡捕前往调查此事。警员将三名朝鲜人带至日本领事馆，分别为：朴志浩（Pak Chi Ho，音译），37岁，住吴淞路565号；林俊白（Lim Jun Bai，音译），28岁，住吴淞路旁长安里36号；李尚龙（Lee Shang Long，音译），22岁。警方调查显示，这三人是应朝鲜人协会的要求前往该会，以解决他们之间的纠纷。引发麻烦的事件发生在12月2日晚，当时林和李访问朴的住所，声称奉朝鲜人协会之命要搜查其住所。搜查进行了，他们发现了4包海洛因，每包重一克，并将其带走。搜查过程中，一个电铃和一些家具被砸坏。尽管朴要求林和李出示警方搜查令，但他们并未出示。

朝鲜人协会副会长李英鲁（Lee Young Ro，音译）先生得知此事后，要求三人到协会解决此事，就在此时，李尚龙开始闹事。领事警察正在对此事作进一步调查。

A Japanese named G. Tahara,
age 34, who was arrested the other day on a charge of
embezzlement, was sentenced to ten days imprisonment at
the Japanese Consular Police Court for a contravention
of the Japanese Consulate regulations.

D. 3104

VICE-ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE LEAVING FOR THE SOUTH

Vice-Admiral Hyakutake,
Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese Third Fleet, will
leave here at 9 a.m. December 9 on the flagship "Idzumo"
on a tour of inspection of Japanese warships stationed
in the South and will return to Shanghai on or about
December 17.

NICHI-NICHI

CHINA REPLIES TO JAPAN'S PROTEST AGAINST
ANTIMONY MONOPOLY

A Rengo Telegram from Tokyo
dated December 8 reports that, acting on the instructions
of the Tokyo Foreign Office, Mr. Takai, Acting Japanese
Consul at Changsha, lodged a protest with the Hunan
Provincial Government against the latter's action in
giving the monopoly of antimony to a British firm known
as Arnhold & Company.

According to a telegram
received by the Tokyo Foreign Office on December 8
Mr. Takai received the following reply from the Hunan
Provincial Government on December 4 regarding the protest:-
"The Hunan Provincial Government has never
given any company the monopoly of antimony as is alleged
by the Japanese Consul. The provincial government has
given a certain firm a commission to deal in antimony
but it does not amount to a monopoly. Any company or
firm can obtain such a commission."

The Japanese Government being
dissatisfied with the explanation of the Hunan Provincial
Government, will lodge a second protest as soon as further
reports are received in the matter in order to maintain
the principle of the open door policy.

《日日新闻》

中国回复日本关于锑垄断的抗议

东京12月8日联合社电称，奉东京外务省指示，日本驻长沙代理领事高井（Takai）先生就湖南省政府将锑的垄断权授予一家名为阿诺德公司（Arnhold & Company）的英国公司的行为，向湖南省政府提出抗议。

根据东京外务省12月8日收到的一份电报，高井先生于12月4日收到湖南省政府对该抗议的如下答复：“湖南省政府从未如日本领事所称，给予任何公司锑的垄断权。省政府已委托某商行经营锑业，但这并不构成垄断。任何公司或商行均可获得此类委托。”

主题（全称） 百武（Hyakutake）海军中将抵达。

制作人 D. S. Umemoto。 转发人 [签名]

关于所附百武（Hyakutake）海军中将（参谋本部次长）抵达的报告，随同前来的有参谋军官南云（Nagumo）和佐藤（Sato）大尉，根据特别股主管的指示进行查询后，已查明百武海军中将及其随从人员将乘坐“上海丸”轮抵达上海，该轮预定于1932年1月19日下午2时40分停靠日本邮船会社码头。

在与第一外遣支队参谋军官及日本海军陆战队面谈时，他们表示不需要警察护卫，但如果能派出一队警察在码头执行特别勤务，他们将不胜感激。

百武海军中将在上海逗留期间，将入住海宁路10号宝裕馆旅馆。

他在上海的日程安排如下：

1月19日：第一外遣支队司令官将于下午6时在闸北波兰花园（Polish Garden，疑为六三花园之误或别称）举行招待会，欢迎百武海军中将。

ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE COMING HERE SOON

Shanghai, Jan. 15

Vice-Admiral Gengo Hyakutake, Assistant Chief of the Naval General Staff, accompanied by Captains Nagumo and Sato, staff officers, left Tokyo this morning for Shanghai and other Yangtze ports to inspect the Japanese naval vessels on patrol duty here, it was learned from official sources today.

Upon arrival in Shanghai, Vice-Admiral Hyakutake will receive a report from Rear-Admiral Shiozawa, commander of the Japanese squadron on the Yangtze, regarding the patrolling duties in this area, including the incidents wherein Japanese bluejackets have been landed ashore because of anti-Japanese violence. He will proceed as far up the river as Hankow and will inspect the different ships stationed or patrolling the river.

His stay in this part of China will probably be about two weeks and he is scheduled to arrive back in Tokyo on or about the 4th of next month. He is also coming with a message of cheer from the Navy Department and the Naval General Staff Office to the officers and sailors on duty here. The work of the Yangtze patrol squadron, as well as the landing party stationed in Shanghai, since the outbreak of the Manchurian incident, during the days when anti-Japanese agitations were especially marked, will be discussed between Rear-Admiral Shiozawa and the visiting officers from Tokyo.--Press Union

百武海军上将即将来此

上海，1月15日

据官方消息今日获悉，海军军令部次长百武元吾（Gengo Hyakutake）海军中将，随同参谋军官南云（Nagumo）和佐藤（Sato）大尉，今晨离开东京前往上海及其他长江港口，视察在此执行巡逻任务的日本海军舰艇。

抵达上海后，百武海军中将将从负责长江防务的日本舰队司令盐泽（Shiozawa）海军少将处听取关于该区域巡逻任务的报告，其中包括因反日暴力事件导致日本水兵登陆上岸的事件。他将溯江而上直至汉口，并视察驻扎或在该江面巡逻的各艘舰艇。

他在中国这一地区的停留时间可能约为两周，计划于下月4日左右返回东京。他还带来了海军部和海军军令部给在此服役的官兵们的慰问信。自满洲事变爆发以来，特别是在反日 agitation（煽动/骚乱）尤为显著的时期，长江巡逻舰队以及驻扎在上海的海军陆战队的工作情况，将在盐泽海军少将与来自东京的来访军官之间进行讨论。--合众通讯社
